fix_choice.chosen: wrapper-level: env-derived TASK_ID that the local kanban doesn't carry is treated as advisory (warn + fall through to unlabelled), not a refusal. Explicit --task / --bundle stay strict (the caller named the id on purpose).
fix_choice.rejected_alternative: harness-level: regression-git-commit-mine.sh scrubs MANAGENT_TASK_ID at the top, like the other three wrapper-using regressions (claim-lifecycle, hook, precommit).
fix_choice.justification: Brief said 'prefer the boundary that also protects the OTHER scripts — this is one instance of environment bleeding across the scratch boundary, and tonight produced three more.' The other three (regression-claim-lifecycle, regression-git-commit-mine-hook, regression-precommit) all already scrub or set MANAGENT_TASK_ID explicitly per arm — the leak class is 'env-bleed across scratch boundary'. A wrapper-level fix catches this class for ALL current callers AND any future regression that creates a scratch repo, so it is structurally safer than a per-script scrub. The alternative heuristic the brief listed ('wrapper ignores MANAGENT_TASK_ID when $REPO != $LIB_DIR/..') would have broken regression-claim-lifecycle (it deliberately invokes the wrapper from a scratch repo with MANAGENT_TASK_ID=TLC-ARM1, which IS in the scratch kanban — that test would have flipped GREEN-with-leak instead of testing the strict refusal). The 'kanban-known id' boundary preserves regression-claim-lifecycle's coverage and removes the leak.

wrapper_change.summary: Track whether TASK_ID came from $MANAGENT_TASK_ID via TASK_ID_FROM_ENV=1. In the scope-resolution block, when gcm_task_bundle fails and TASK_ID_FROM_ENV=1, warn on stderr and clear TASK_ID (so the rest of the wrapper proceeds as unlabelled — no scope check, no claim-status check). When gcm_task_bundle fails and TASK_ID_FROM_ENV=0, the existing strict refusal stands (the caller passed --task on purpose).
wrapper_change.warning_text: git-commit-mine: NOTE — $MANAGENT_TASK_ID=<id> is not in <repo>/docs/infra/managent/tasks.json; treating the call as unlabelled. (a regression harness invoking the wrapper from a scratch repo with the parent's env inherits MANAGENT_TASK_ID=<id>, which the scratch kanban cannot resolve — T369 / T454.)
